job.title: Geologist/Sr. Geologist
job.description:
Geologist / Senior Geologist – Geothermal (EGS)

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Geologist / Senior Geologist with extensive geothermal exploration and development experience within the Basin and Range geologic province of the western United States.

This position supports geothermal exploration, subsurface characterization, well planning, reservoir development, and operations, with a focus on Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS).

The ideal candidate brings strong expertise in Basin and Range geology, structural geology, fault systems, geothermal resource characterization, and subsurface conceptual modeling. Working within a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, this individual will provide technical leadership across geothermal projects from initial exploration through development and operations.

Essential Responsibilities

Geothermal Exploration & Geological Evaluation

  • Lead geological evaluations supporting geothermal exploration, appraisal, development, and operations within the Basin and Range province.
  • Apply expertise in regional tectonics, extensional fault systems, structural geology, and geothermal resource characterization to evaluate prospects.
  • Conduct geological mapping, structural interpretations, and subsurface evaluations to identify geothermal resources and assess development potential.
  • Evaluate geological risks, uncertainties, and opportunities while developing technical recommendations for exploration and development.

Subsurface Characterization & Modeling

  • Develop and maintain integrated subsurface conceptual models incorporating geological, geophysical, geochemical, and well data.
  • Analyze downhole petrophysical and image logs to characterize lithology, fractures, rock properties, and subsurface conditions.
  • Integrate active and/or passive seismic survey results into geological interpretations and subsurface conceptual models.
  • Characterize fault systems, fracture networks, and structural controls influencing geothermal reservoir performance.
  • Support subsurface stress characterization, heat flow interpretation, and reservoir modeling activities.

Well Planning, Drilling & Reservoir Development

  • Provide geological expertise supporting geothermal well planning, drilling, and development, including horizontal wells.
  • Collaborate with drilling and reservoir engineering teams to optimize well placement, trajectories, and subsurface targeting.
  • Support geothermal reservoir testing, characterization, and development activities.
  • Contribute geological expertise to EGS development, hydraulic stimulation, and reservoir optimization initiatives.
  • Manage geological activities across multiple geothermal prospects from exploration through development and operations.

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

  • Lead multidisciplinary technical initiatives involving geology, geophysics, drilling, reservoir engineering, and operations.
  • Support geophysical survey planning, execution, and interpretation.
  • Prepare geological reports, technical presentations, subsurface models, and recommendations for project leadership.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders, external consultants, and technical partners on development projects, permitting, and due diligence.
  • Maintain accurate geological databases, well information, and technical documentation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve geological workflows, modeling techniques, and EGS development practices.
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship while maintaining a strong commitment to workplace safety.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • Master’s degree in Geology, Geological Sciences, Geophysics, Geological Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional geoscience experience.
  • Extensive, demonstrated geothermal exploration and/or development experience specifically within the Basin and Range geologic province is required.
  • Strong understanding of Basin and Range geology, including extensional tectonics, fault systems, structural geology, and geothermal resource characteristics.
  • Experience supporting geothermal exploration, subsurface characterization, and development projects.

Required Technical Skills

  • Horizontal Well Drilling: Experience planning and supporting horizontal well drilling operations.
  • Seismic Integration: Experience integrating active and/or passive seismic surveys into subsurface conceptual models.
  • Petrophysics: Hands-on experience analyzing downhole petrophysical logs and borehole image logs.
  • Subsurface Characterization: Ability to interpret well logs to characterize geological conditions, fractures, and rock properties.
  • Structural Geology: Demonstrated experience in field geological mapping and structural geology.
  • Geological Modeling: Experience developing subsurface conceptual models using integrated geological, geophysical, and well datasets.
  • Technical Software: Proficiency with relevant geological mapping, interpretation, and modeling applications, including ArcGIS, ENVI, Global Mapper, Petrel, Leapfrog, WellCAD, or Surfer.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in a relevant geoscience discipline.
  • Direct experience with Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) exploration, development, or operations.
  • Experience characterizing subsurface stress distribution, orientation, and geological stress regimes.
  • Experience modeling fracture initiation, propagation, and interaction based on rock properties and geological conditions.
  • Experience supporting hydraulic fracturing or geothermal reservoir stimulation programs.
  • Experience characterizing igneous and metamorphic geological environments.
  • Experience modeling geothermal heat flow, subsurface heat sources, and interpreting surface heat flow indicators.
  • Experience interpreting magnetotelluric, gravity, and other geophysical datasets.
  • Experience with quantitative analysis, data science, or advanced geoscience modeling.
  • Project management experience; CAPM or PMP certification preferred.

Additional Skills & Requirements

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical decision-making capabilities.
  • Ability to independently manage multiple projects and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including technical reporting and presentations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and geological data management systems.
  • Ability to evaluate geological uncertainties and communicate technical recommendations.
  • Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record.

Physical Requirements & Travel

  • Ability to work in office, geothermal power plant, wellfield, and active drilling environments.
  • Ability to access remote field locations and navigate steep, rugged terrain in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to safely operate four-wheel-drive vehicles and wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
  • Ability to perform extended computer-based work and periodically lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Willingness to travel up to 30%, including occasional international travel.

Salary Range: $170,000 - $230,000

job.description:
VP of Supply Chain

The Vice President of Supply Chain is a hands-on executive leader accountable for enterprise-wide supply chain performance, including purchasing, procurement, global and domestic strategic sourcing, supply planning, inventory management, material requirements, supplier performance, and material availability. As a member of the executive leadership team reporting directly to the CEO, this leader pairs strong executive presence and poise with a highly visible, floor-driven operating style.

The VP will build and lead a world-class supply chain that improves material availability, reduces inventory and working capital, strengthens supplier performance, lowers total cost, and establishes the operating discipline needed to support profitable growth. Success requires both enterprise-level leadership and personal involvement in the critical details that drive manufacturing performance.

This role carries direct accountability for more than $50 million in annual spend and approximately $35 million in inventory, with a clear mandate to reduce inventory while improving material availability and customer service. The VP will personally drive critical initiatives while building and overseeing a capable supply chain organization.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the full purchasing and procurement organization, including global and domestic strategic sourcing, supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, supplier development, and ongoing supplier performance management.
  • Personally lead high-impact sourcing, negotiation, and supplier-management activities while overseeing and developing the supply chain team; this is not a purely delegative executive role.
  • Own supply planning within the SIOP process. Demand planning remains under the Production VP; the VP of Supply Chain translates approved demand into executable supply and material plans.
  • Ensure materials are available at every required point of use to support production schedules, customer commitments, aftermarket needs, and business growth.
  • Own material requirements planning and inventory strategy, policy, execution, and performance across the enterprise.
  • Manage approximately $35 million of inventory with the explicit objective of reducing working capital while simultaneously improving availability and service.
  • Manage and influence more than $50 million in annual external spend, delivering sustainable cost, quality, delivery, lead-time, and commercial improvements.
  • Establish sourcing strategies that balance cost, quality, continuity of supply, lead time, capacity, geopolitical exposure, and total landed cost.
  • Lead supplier negotiations and make final supplier-selection and sourcing decisions within delegated authority. Final authority is up to $1 million; commitments above $1 million require CEO/CFO signoff.
  • Build strong supplier relationships while holding suppliers accountable for delivery, quality, cost, responsiveness, capacity, and corrective action.
  • Partner closely with Production, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Commercial, and Aftermarket leaders to resolve constraints and improve end-to-end flow.
  • Develop the supply chain organization, including structure, talent, succession, standard work, accountability, and performance management.
  • Maintain a strong operating cadence using data, KPIs, supplier reviews, shortage management, and root-cause problem solving.
  • Spend meaningful time on the manufacturing floor and with suppliers, directly engaging in operating issues.

Qualifications

  • Significant progressive leadership experience in supply chain, procurement, sourcing, materials, and planning within a complex discrete manufacturing environment.
  • Direct, hands-on manufacturing/production operations management experience is mandatory. Candidates must have personally managed manufacturing or production operations in addition to supply chain leadership.
  • Demonstrated responsibility for substantial external spend, complex supplier negotiations, and material/inventory performance.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead both strategically and tactically - personally solving problems, negotiating, visiting suppliers, and working on the manufacturing floor.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, including working capital, cost, cash, inventory economics, make/buy decisions, and total cost of ownership.
  • Executive presence, poise, sound judgment, and the ability to communicate effectively with the CEO, executive team, board/investor stakeholders, suppliers, and frontline employees.
  • Proven ability to build, lead, and develop teams while maintaining clear accountability for results.
  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 20% domestically and 10% internationally
  • High ownership and bias for action
  • Visible, hands-on operating leadership
  • Strong negotiation and supplier-management capability
  • Data-driven and financially disciplined
  • Direct, clear communicator with strong executive presence
  • Collaborative across functions while willing to make difficult decisions
  • Develops people and raises organizational capability

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Director of News

Location: Remote – United States or Latin America

Employment Type: Full-time, Exempt

Compensation: $120,000–$145,000 base salary

About the Organization

Our client is a growing international nonprofit media organization working across the United States, Latin America, Europe, and the Middle East.

The organization focuses on journalism, international affairs, media engagement, and producing relevant, accurate, and impactful content for diverse audiences. Its work spans traditional journalism and digital media, with an emphasis on timely reporting, informed perspectives, and addressing misinformation.

Position Overview

Our client is seeking an experienced Director of News to lead its editorial strategy, newsroom operations, and digital content development.

This is a senior editorial leadership position for an accomplished journalist who combines strong newsroom experience, exceptional editorial judgment, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of the modern digital media landscape.

The Director of News will oversee the organization's editorial agenda, manage journalists and multidisciplinary content teams, supervise breaking news coverage, and develop strategies to expand audience reach, engagement, and impact.

The successful candidate will understand how to identify important stories, establish editorial priorities, lead coverage in fast-moving news environments, and translate audience data into effective editorial and distribution strategies.

This person will work closely with executive leadership to shape the organization's editorial direction and strengthen its overall media presence.

Editorial Strategy & Leadership

  • Establish editorial priorities and develop a consistent, proactive news agenda.
  • Lead and develop multidisciplinary teams of journalists, editors, producers, and digital professionals.
  • Maintain high standards of editorial quality, accuracy, independence, and journalistic integrity.

Newsroom Management & Breaking News

Digital Strategy & Audience Growth

  • Lead multiplatform distribution strategies across YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and other relevant channels.
  • Analyze audience behavior and identify opportunities to reach new audiences.
  • Incorporate digital trends and evolving consumption habits into editorial planning.
  • Balance journalistic relevance and quality with digital performance objectives.

Analytics, KPIs & Performance

  • Establish editorial and digital performance indicators.
  • Use audience analytics and performance dashboards to guide editorial decisions.
  • Monitor content performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Translate data into actionable recommendations for content strategy and resource allocation.
  • Prepare performance reports and communicate results to executive leadership.
  • Promote continuous improvement through experimentation and measurable outcomes.

Institutional & Strategic Collaboration

  • Work closely with executive leadership on editorial priorities and organizational strategy.
  • Coordinate with other departments to support institutional objectives.
  • Develop editorial partnerships and strategic collaborations with media organizations.
  • Represent the organization with media partners, institutions, and international organizations when appropriate.

  • Demonstrated experience working in professional newsrooms and leading or coordinating editorial teams.
  • Proven experience managing complex news coverage and breaking news.
  • Experience managing multidisciplinary teams of journalists, editors, producers, and digital professionals.
  • Demonstrated success developing editorial strategies and driving digital audience growth.
  • Experience using audience analytics, performance metrics, and KPIs to inform editorial decisions.
  • Strong understanding of digital media platforms, multiplatform distribution, and modern news consumption.
  • Excellent editorial judgment and the ability to prioritize stories and make decisions under pressure.
  • Strong understanding of fact-checking, source verification, and journalistic ethics.
  • Professional fluency in both Spanish and English.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background with established and respected media organizations.
  • Experience in digital newsroom transformation or editorial innovation.
  • Experience developing strategic media partnerships.
  • Familiarity with fact-checking initiatives and combating misinformation.
  • Experience with organizations focused on social impact, democracy, human rights, or international affairs.
  • Experience developing content for multicultural and international audiences.
  • Additional language skills.

Ideal Candidate

This is an opportunity for an experienced media professional to take ownership of a growing international organization's editorial direction and make a meaningful contribution to its reach and influence.

job.description:
Senior Social Content & Creative Lead

LOCATION: Scottsdale, AZ — In Office

TRAVEL: Periodic

COMPENSATION $100,000-$120,000

REPORTS TO: Operations Leadership

Role Purpose

Own the organic social and content strategy from idea through publication, while leading the Creative Production function. This person should be a strong strategist and operator who personally works in the platforms, runs the calendar, makes publishing decisions, directs creative resources, reviews performance and adjusts the plan. They do not need to be the primary videographer or editor; the team already has two videographers and a graphic designer.

Important: This is not a “make the deck and hand it off” role. The best candidate is a working owner: strategic enough to set direction, operational enough to publish and optimize, and senior enough to lead the creative resources around them.

What This Person Owns

  • Organic social strategy and platform strategy across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and other relevant channels.
  • National content/editorial calendar, including what gets posted, where, when and why.
  • Hands-on scheduling and publishing; writing/refining captions, tags, collaboration posts and platform setup.
  • Creative priorities and briefs for the videographers, graphic designer and Social Media & Content Specialist.
  • Recurring series, campaigns, executive/personality-led content and nationalization of strong local stories.
  • Performance analysis, testing and optimization based on reach, watch time, engagement, shares, saves and audience growth.
  • Brand consistency across social and creative output while keeping content native to each platform.
  • Day-to-day leadership of the Creative Production function and accountability for work getting across the finish line.

Candidate Profile

A hands-on senior social/content operator with strong strategic judgment. They can build a plan, but they also enjoy

executing it. They should be comfortable opening the publishing tool, making the call on a caption, adjusting the

calendar, reviewing a cut, interpreting performance, and moving quickly when the opportunity changes.

Motorcycle fit: riding experience is a major plus and strong preference for this seat because cultural fluency matters,

but it is not an absolute gate if the candidate is otherwise exceptional.

Must-Haves

  • Meaningful experience owning organic social strategy for a brand, media property, sports/lifestyle organization or creator-driven business.
  • Direct experience managing social calendars and personally scheduling/publishing content.
  • Strong knowledge of Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube, including how content behavior differs by platform.
  • Evidence of measurable organic audience or engagement growth.
  • Strong writing/editorial judgment and the ability to shape hooks, copy, concepts and content priorities.
  • Experience directing or leading creative resources such as videographers, editors or designers.
  • Strong analytics instincts; can explain what changed because of what the data showed.
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment without separating “strategy” from “execution.”

Strong Plus

• Active motorcycle rider strongly preferred. Do not automatically reject an exceptional social/content strategist who is not currently a rider,

but the candidate should demonstrate genuine enthusiasm for and the ability to become deeply immersed in motorcycle culture.

  • Experience with executive/on-camera content and recurring social series.
  • Experience building a social/content operation rather than inheriting a fully mature one.

Likely Dealbreakers

  • Candidate describes themselves primarily as a creative director, agency manager or brand strategist who delegates execution.
  • Limited direct experience working inside social publishing platforms.
  • Portfolio is mostly polished campaign work with little evidence of ongoing organic social execution.
  • Cannot clearly explain how they used performance data to change content or distribution decisions.
  • Treats posting, QA, captions or platform setup as work that should always be handled by junior staff.

Position Overview

Our client, a growing family-owned industrial manufacturer and distributor, is seeking a Director of Inventory Management to provide leadership and oversight of inventory across three U.S. manufacturing and distribution locations.

This is a newly created leadership position designed to support significant organizational growth and increasing operational complexity.

The Director of Inventory Management will oversee inventory across raw materials, work in process, and finished goods while helping determine how customer demand and manufacturing capacity should be allocated across the company’s facilities.

This individual will work closely with manufacturing, distribution, operations, sales, scheduling, and other internal teams to balance inventory availability, production capacity, customer lead times, ongoing business needs, and large project requirements.

The successful candidate will combine strong inventory-management expertise with analytical ability, operational judgment, leadership skills, and the ability to build strong relationships across multiple functions and locations.

  • Lead inventory management strategy and execution across three manufacturing and distribution locations.
  • Provide oversight of raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, and associated inventory-control activities.
  • Maintain strong inventory-control practices, including cycle counting, inventory accuracy, and identification and resolution of inventory discrepancies.
  • Evaluate inventory availability, manufacturing capacity, equipment capabilities, and customer requirements to help determine where orders should be produced.
  • Coordinate inventory and capacity requirements across multiple facilities to support efficient product flow and customer service.
  • Balance large project requirements with normal customer demand, available inventory, production capacity, and lead-time commitments.
  • Partner closely with manufacturing, distribution, operations, sales, and scheduling teams to align inventory and production priorities.
  • Improve inventory visibility, processes, controls, and cross-site coordination as the organization continues to grow.
  • Use inventory and operational data to identify constraints, risks, trends, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Lead and develop an inventory organization of approximately 10 team members, including scheduling and data-focused functions.
  • Build strong working relationships across all three operating locations and serve as a key inventory-management partner to organizational leadership.

Qualifications

  • Progressive experience in inventory management, inventory control, supply chain, distribution, or a related operational function.
  • Strong hands-on understanding of inventory-control principles, including cycle counts and inventory accuracy.
  • Experience managing meaningful physical inventory within a manufacturing, industrial distribution, or comparable supply-chain environment.
  • Experience working with raw materials, work in process, finished goods, or similarly complex inventory flows.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively across operations, manufacturing, distribution, scheduling, sales, and other business functions.
  • Leadership experience with the ability to develop employees, establish accountability, and guide teams through growth and change.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to use operational and inventory data to make sound business decisions.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to balance competing priorities in a growing, fast-moving operational environment.

Preferred Experience

  • Cost accounting knowledge or experience.
  • Multi-site inventory-management experience.
  • Experience with production scheduling, capacity planning, or inventory allocation across multiple facilities.
  • Experience within wire and cable, electrical products, metals, industrial manufacturing, industrial distribution, or a related environment.
  • Experience balancing large project or customer requirements with ongoing production and inventory needs.
  • Demonstrated success improving inventory accuracy, controls, visibility, or planning processes.

Leadership Profile

The ideal candidate will be a collaborative, hands-on leader who understands that effective inventory management extends beyond maintaining stock levels.

This individual should be able to connect inventory availability, manufacturing capacity, customer demand, production priorities, and broader business needs while building effective relationships across the organization.

The company values leaders who demonstrate sound judgment and accountability; work effectively as part of a team; and are interested in building a long-term career with the organization.

Data Engineer - Denver, CO

Why This Role Exists

We are building the next generation of an AI-driven data and intelligence platform within a high-volume, multi-tenant SaaS environment. Every transaction and system integration generates valuable data, and our ability to turn that information into reliable reporting, analytics, and AI-powered insights depends on a modern, scalable data foundation.

We are looking for a Data Engineer to architect, build, and operate the analytical data ecosystem that supports today's reporting needs while powering tomorrow's AI and intelligence capabilities.

This is a hands-on builder role on a small, highly collaborative engineering team. You will own data pipelines end to end—from ingestion and transformation through the models, APIs, reports, and AI applications that consume the data. You'll also have a meaningful voice in the architectural decisions shaping the future of the platform.

Scope & Scale

You'll work in a complex production environment that includes:

  • Thousands of tenants with isolated databases and tenant-specific configurations.
  • Data pipelines spanning multiple integration domains and connectivity methods, including REST, SOAP, and event-driven architectures.
  • A large semantic layer supporting business intelligence, self-service reporting, operational teams, and strategic partners.
  • A modern lakehouse architecture using bronze, silver, and gold layers on Apache Iceberg.
  • Production AI capabilities whose tools, context, and intelligence depend directly on the quality and reliability of the data you provide.

What You'll Own

AWS Data Workloads

Architect, build, and operationalize pipelines and storage using technologies such as AWS Glue, Athena, S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, and Step Functions. Depending on the workload, you'll also work with technologies such as Timestream, Flink, and Kafka.

Lakehouse Architecture

Build and optimize bronze, silver, and gold data layers using Apache Iceberg. You'll own table design, partitioning, compaction, and storage-format decisions involving technologies such as Parquet, Iceberg, and ORC.

Data Models & Access

Develop trusted data models used by analysts, reports, applications, and AI capabilities. Build secure data-access APIs using Java and/or Python and implement real-time streaming where appropriate.

Pipeline Reliability

Establish monitoring, alerting, logging, freshness checks, and completeness controls that identify pipeline problems before they impact users.

Anomaly Detection & Data Quality

Apply statistical and machine-learning approaches to monitor data quality and integration activity, allowing spikes, drops, anomalies, and silent failures to surface quickly.

Forecasting & Predictive Analytics

Develop models in Python using technologies such as scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy to support forecasting and predictive capabilities.

Governance & Security

Help ensure data remains secure and appropriately isolated through SSL/TLS, client authentication, access auditing, and tenant-level controls.

Cross-Functional Delivery

Partner with engineers, product managers, analysts, and AI-focused teams to translate business and technical requirements into scalable, secure, high-quality data solutions.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days

You'll learn the platform, integration domains, and semantic layer well enough to trace key metrics back to their source systems.

You'll take ownership of production reporting pipelines, strengthen freshness and completeness monitoring where needed, and ship your first production change to the lakehouse.

You'll also develop a clear technical point of view regarding the ingestion and modeling patterns the organization should standardize going forward.

First Year

The lakehouse architecture will be operating in production with mature bronze, silver, and gold layers that you helped build or strengthen.

Production pipeline issues will increasingly be identified through proactive monitoring rather than user reports.

You'll have delivered at least one forecasting or anomaly-detection model that is actively used within the product or business operations.

Just as importantly, the architectural and engineering patterns you establish will provide a foundation future data engineers can build upon.

Hands-On Expectations

This is a highly technical, hands-on engineering position.

Your time will generally be divided among:

  • 70%: Building and operating pipelines, data models, APIs, and monitoring.
  • 20%: Data architecture and technical design with platform and AI teams.
  • 10%: Working with analysts and product teams on requirements and enablement.

You should expect to write and ship production code every week.

What You Bring

Must Have

  • Extensive experience architecting, building, and operationalizing data workloads on AWS, particularly Athena, Glue, S3, and DynamoDB.
  • Deep understanding of high-performance analytical data platforms and distributed systems.
  • Strong knowledge of modern data formats and technologies such as Parquet, Apache Iceberg, and ORC.
  • Expertise building services and APIs on top of data platforms using Java and/or Python.
  • Strong experience with data modeling, data-access API design, and production monitoring and alerting.
  • Hands-on Python experience for analytics and machine learning using pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn.
  • Experience applying statistical or machine-learning approaches to anomaly detection.
  • Ability to clearly document pipelines, data definitions, architectural decisions, and production incidents for both technical and business audiences.
  • Strong problem-solving and collaboration skills with the ability to thrive on a fast-moving, highly accountable engineering team.

Strongly Preferred

  • Lakehouse experience using Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or Apache Hudi, including medallion-style data architectures.
  • Production experience with real-time streaming technologies such as Flink, Kafka, or Kinesis.
  • Experience building data infrastructure that supports LLM agents or AI-powered product features, including tool-facing APIs, retrieval architectures, or feature stores.
  • Experience with multi-tenant SaaS data architecture, including tenant isolation, row-level security, and tenant-specific configuration.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with complex transactional or highly integrated SaaS platforms.
  • Power BI, Amazon Quick, or similar semantic modeling experience.
  • Experience with dbt-style transformation workflows.
  • Infrastructure-as-code experience using AWS CDK or CloudFormation.
  • Experience implementing CI/CD practices for data pipelines.

Technology Environment

Data Platform:

Amazon Athena / Presto / Trino SQL, AWS Glue, Amazon S3, Apache Iceberg, DynamoDB, Lambda, Step Functions

Streaming & Time Series:

Timestream, Flink, Kafka

Languages & Machine Learning:

Python, Java, SQL, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn

Reliability & Governance:

CloudWatch, OpenTelemetry, data freshness and completeness monitoring, SSL/TLS, access auditing

Analytics & AI:

Business intelligence platforms, semantic modeling tools, LLM/AI agents, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled data applications

How You'll Use AI

AI is an active part of the engineering workflow, not an experimental side project. You'll be expected to use modern AI development tools to increase engineering velocity while maintaining a high standard for accuracy and production quality.

Examples include:

  • Drafting and testing pipeline code, SQL, and data-quality checks with AI assistance, followed by validation against trusted production data.
  • Generating lineage and documentation directly from data models to keep mappings between source systems, reporting, and AI applications current.
  • Summarizing pipeline incidents into useful root-cause documentation and actionable runbooks.
  • Building the tables, APIs, data models, and context layers that production AI capabilities depend on.
  • Rapidly prototyping forecasting and anomaly-detection approaches and evaluating their effectiveness against real-world outcomes.

The goal isn't simply to use AI tools—it's to build the reliable data foundation that production AI depends on.

You'll work at the intersection of data engineering, cloud architecture, analytics, machine learning, and production AI, with direct ownership over systems that have a meaningful impact on the broader product.

You will learn the platform, understand the existing monolith and modernization roadmap, and take ownership of your assigned technical areas and their production support responsibilities.

You’ll begin leading design and code reviews, establish engineering expectations with the team, ship a meaningful production change in your primary technology stack, and develop the design plan for an upcoming domain extraction.

Success will include leading at least one significant domain extraction from the monolith through dual-write, traffic splitting, validation, and clean production cutover.

You’ll help establish independently deployable frontend modules, ensure performance standards are met, implement reliable tool contracts for AI agents interacting with your domain, and create a cohesive delivery cadence across onshore and offshore engineering resources.

Hands-On Expectations

This is a senior individual contributor role, not a management role.

The majority of your time will be spent working directly with technology—writing production code, creating design documentation, reviewing pull requests, leading technical reviews, and owning production cutovers.

You will also be responsible for cross-team technical contracts, production incidents, on-call ownership, and mentoring engineers.

  • Python

  • Full-stack delivery experience, including frontend and backend development within the same product area.
